content.text:
Both the dashboard and the alert rule exist, and the rule is enabled.

**Data view findings:** `kibana_sample_data_logs` has 14,074 requests from 1,001 distinct client IPs (`clientip`). Status codes are 200 (12,832), 404 (801) and 503 (441). The top destination countries are CN, IN and US. The timestamps run from 2026-10-04 to 2026-12-03, so part of the data is in the future relative to today (2026-10-11).

**Dashboard:** "EFF-46e81178 Web logs overview" (id `eff-46e81178-web-logs-overview-2ad0be6db619`) has five panels:
- Total requests (metric)
- Requests over time (area, date histogram on `@timestamp`)
- Requests by HTTP response code (pie, on `response.keyword`)
- 5xx responses (metric, filtered to `response.keyword` = 503)
- Top countries by requests (bar, on `geo.dest`)

I set the dashboard time range to 2026-10-01 through 2026-12-31 so it shows all the sample data. The default of the last 7 days would show nothing.

**Alert rule:** "EFF-46e81178 5xx spike" (id `b7d4f9e3-61f2-44f6-b827-6857476e5941`) is an Elasticsearch query rule:
- Runs every 1m over a 5m window on `@timestamp`.
- Fires when the count is greater than 10.
- The query matches `response.keyword` with the wildcard `5??`, so it covers every 5xx code, not only 503.
- Consumer `stackAlerts`, enabled. The rule status is `ok`, and alerting health reports `ok`.

**Choices I made:**
- I used the Kibana MCP tools rather than the raw API. `KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY` isn't set in my shell, so I didn't call the REST API directly.
- I created the rule disabled and then enabled it in a separate step.
- The "5xx spike" alert has no action connector, so it records alerts but sends no notifications. I can add one if you want notifications.
